title: JITServe: SLO-aware LLM Serving with Imprecise Request Information
technique: just-in-time SLO-aware scheduling using imprecise (predicted) output length and dependency info: grouped margin goodput maximization (GMAX) allocates just enough bandwidth per request to meet its SLO, then groups requests by length for batch efficiency

optimized_metrics.evidence: the first SLO-aware LLM serving system designed to maximize service goodput (e.g., the number of tokens meeting request SLOs) across diverse workloads.

headline_claim.text: JITServe improves service goodput by 1.4x-6.3x, alternatively achieving 28.5%-83.2% resource savings, compared to state-of-the-art designs.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: maximizing service goodput (i.e., effective service throughput like the total number of tokens that meet request SLOs)
Latency-sensitive requests: measured as the number of tokens delivered within the expected timeline [71, 75]. Specifically, token i counts toward goodput if it finishes by TTFT_SLO + i x TBT_SLO.
metric_definitions.notes: per-token timeline goodput (token-level SLO), akin to a QoE-style deadline per token

metric_definitions.definition_quote: Deadline-sensitive requests: measured as the total number of tokens, including input and output, if the request completes before its deadline; zero otherwise

(1) Token-level goodput: the number of tokens meeting SLO requirements, following popular SLO preferences; and (2) Request-level goodput: the number of requests meeting the SLO requirements. We also report traditional metrics such as TTFT, TBT, and throughput for performance breakdown.
metric_definitions.notes: two goodput variants evaluated; JITServe is agnostic to goodput definition

metric_definitions.definition_quote: low end-to-end latency (i.e., E2EL like time-to-last-token)

slo_spec: SLOs set from P95 latencies measured on 1K DeepSeek API calls: latency-sensitive ~2 s TTFT and ~100 ms TBT; deadline-sensitive E2EL 20 s; compound E2EL = 20 s x number of stages. 1:1:1 mix of the three request patterns by default; best-effort requests get a default deadline.
load_regime: trace replay (Microsoft LLM serving trace scaled to cluster; Poisson ablation); >10K requests over >=1 hour
tradeoff_acknowledged: Grouping cutoff p trades batch-length homogeneity (efficiency) vs diluting group goodput; goodput-only scheduling can be unfair (fairness-adjustable priority); aggressive optimization can sacrifice a small subset of requests (shown not to occur).
workloads: chat, deep research, agentic pipelines, code generation; request mix from LMSYS-Chat statistics and a user study; Microsoft serving trace
extractor_notes: Goodput is explicitly parametric (provider-defined); evaluated as token-level and request-level variants; deadline-sensitive goodput counts input+output tokens. TTFT/TBT SLO as per-token timeline (token i due at TTFT_SLO + i*TBT_SLO) - not a percentile of TBT. SLO thresholds derived from P95 of DeepSeek API.

tail_audit.metrics: SLO thresholds calibrated from P95 of measured API latency; P50/P95 reported
